PullRequest.Title: feat(terminal): add New Terminal to the editor new tab button
PullRequest.Body:

Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/347849

- Add a **New Terminal** entry to the new tab (+) button at the end of the editor tab bar (`workbench.editor.newTabButton`), listed after the existing entries.
- Like the other entries, it opens a terminal editor in the editor group of the + that was pressed, after that group's last tab, and focuses the terminal. Picked from the + of an inactive group, it opens there and activates that group.
- List it only while terminal processes are supported (`terminalProcessSupported`), the same condition as **New Terminal** in the tab bar context menu.
- Add an optional `index` to `TerminalEditorLocation`, which `TerminalEditorService.openEditor` passes on to the editor service, so that the terminal editor opens after the last tab rather than next to the active one. Existing callers don't set it, so where they open terminal editors is unchanged.

### How to test

1. Set `"workbench.editor.newTabButton": true`.
2. Open two files and select the first one.
3. Press the + after the last tab: the menu lists **New Terminal** after the other entries.
4. Pick **New Terminal**: a terminal editor opens after the last tab, not next to the selected file, and the terminal has keyboard focus.
5. Split the editor, press the + of the group that is not active and pick **New Terminal**: the terminal opens at the end of that group, which becomes active.
6. Open a + menu again: **New Terminal** is listed first as recently used.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalActions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalEditorService.test.ts`: 16 passing, 3 of them new. Each new test fails with its production change reverted.
- `./scripts/test.sh --isolate --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalActions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalEditorService.test.ts`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/**/*.test.js"`: 648 passing, 4 pending.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/test/browser/newTabButtonActions.test.ts`: 4 passing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --web --headless <scenario>` against this branch, with real terminals through the dev server: all 6 steps passed. The menu listed `New Untitled Text File | New Markdown Document | New Chat Editor | New Terminal`; picking New Terminal with `first.txt` active gave the tabs `first.txt, last.txt, terminal (active)`; picking it from the + of the inactive group of a split opened it at the end of that group and activated it. The desktop build was not driven end to end.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The entry shape, a `<command id>.fromNewTabButton` action with a `when` for the availability of its feature that opens its tab with the given options, follows [`NewChatEditorFromNewTabButtonAction`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatActions.ts#L867-L883) and [`OpenIntegratedBrowserFromNewTabButtonAction`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/features/browserTabManagementFeatures.ts#L574-L594), on the contract of [`NewTabButtonEntryAction`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/newTabButton.ts#L33-L70): open in the group of the button, after its last tab.
- Creating the terminal editor with `createTerminal({ location: { viewColumn: editorGroupToColumn(...) } })` and then `focusWhenReady()` comes from [`CreateTerminalEditorSameGroup`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalActions.ts#L328-L343). `viewColumn` is a column, which [`TerminalService._getEditorOptions`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts#L1266-L1278) maps back to its group.
- The `terminalProcessSupported` condition comes from **New Terminal** in the [tab bar context menu](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalMenus.ts#L218-L226).
- Passing `index` on follows how [`TerminalEditorService.openEditor`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorService.ts#L144-L165) already passes on `preserveFocus` and `auxiliary`.
- The entry tests are copied semantically from the [new tab button entry tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3471806d1de1a84c8984de543239b5a8a4b5a91b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/test/browser/newTabButtonActions.test.ts#L28-L71): the `when` of the setting, and running an entry from the button of the second group.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench registration and displaying the editor new-tab menu, including disabled settings and unsupported terminal processes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration constructs one action descriptor. Menu display evaluates its context expression and renders one additional entry; ITerminalService is obtained only when the entry runs. No terminal initialization or process launch is required to display the menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing recent-entry storage access and menu telemetry service calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing recent-entry lookup per action-list retrieval, one stored recent command ID per menu, and existing opened/picked/dismissed telemetry events. Adding the terminal entry does not add a storage key or increase events per interaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same control performed these operations for the existing new-tab entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Recent-entry lookup participates in building the menu; telemetry calls are not awaited. No new persistence or network wait is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of editor groups and menu entries: one additional lightweight menu action per applicable group, not one terminal per group or tab.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous action registration and menu construction; no added asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The availability condition reads existing configuration/context keys. Menu display does not inspect terminal profiles or initialize terminal caches. Recent selection continues to overwrite the existing single menu-specific value.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the new action constructor, NewTabButtonEntryAction, registration call, imported helper, and menu control. Terminal service access is confined to openTab.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu construction was not profiled; the diff adds only a bounded action descriptor and entry.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: heavyweight work remains deferred until an explicit terminal-creation request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and focus a local terminal editor from the new-tab button in an active or inactive editor group
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The base action activates the requested group, computes its final tab index, and invokes createTerminal once. Creation uses the existing profile/configuration path and opens one terminal editor. The action waits for xterm readiness and attachment to focus it; shell usability additionally requires the existing asynchronous backend creation/start path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover configured/detected profiles through the existing terminal backend
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-discovery operation per executed throttled refresh, returning the profile collection together, not one call per profile, tab, or editor group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The button had no terminal action. Existing CreateTerminalEditor and CreateTerminalEditorSameGroup already used this same discovery path with the same refresh policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold creation can await profilesReady. Cached profiles are available immediately on warm creation, though getters can still schedule the existing throttled refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain launch environments and create a local pty through the existing proxy
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Environment getters are memoized; one backend createProcess request per requested new native terminal, independent of existing tab/group counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent existing terminal-editor commands performed the same environment and pty operations once per new terminal; this PR adds a UI trigger, not additional operations per terminal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Environment readiness and pty creation precede shell startup. This work starts only after the user selects New Terminal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shell start per successful native-terminal creation, without a loop over existing terminals, tabs, or groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing terminal-editor creation workflow started one shell through the identical process manager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the requested shell to become usable; not on menu-display or workbench-registration paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K explicit terminal-creation commands create K instances. Group conversion inspects G groups; the insertion index is group.count rather than a scan that launches work for E existing tabs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One createTerminal call per action invocation. Xterm initialization and editor opening follow existing asynchronous scheduling. TerminalEditorService awaits its previously recorded editor-open request, but this is not a global process-launch limiter; separate explicit commands can overlap as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Xterm constructor loading shares a cached promise. Profile state/readiness and the two-second refresh throttle are unchanged. Local environment getters retain their memoization. Editor inputs remain cached by resource path and removed by the existing close lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the action through group conversion, createTerminal, _createTerminal, openEditor, TerminalInstance construction/readiness, process manager, and local backend.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold profile discovery and shell startup duration depend on machine and configuration; no runtime measurements were taken.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the required existing creation work is invoked once, and optional index forwarding only changes insertion position.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a terminal editor in a remote workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After selection, the unchanged creation pipeline resolves profiles/environment and remote configuration, constructs the launch payload, issues a remote create-process request, and starts the pty. Focus separately waits for existing xterm/attachment readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use existing remote profile/environment services and request remote terminal creation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing grouped profile refreshes and a bounded set of environment/service requests per creation; one remote createProcess request per native terminal. No requests are issued per existing editor tab or group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The button lacked this entry; existing terminal-editor commands reached these same remote services with the same arguments and scheduling apart from editor placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required launch inputs and remote process creation precede shell usability. None are issued solely to display the new menu entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve launch variables and serialize configuration, workspace folders, and environment collections for the remote channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch payload per requested terminal; size scales with existing launch configuration, workspace-folder collection, and environment collections, not editor-tab count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical payload preparation occurred for existing remote terminal-editor creation. The new index remains in editor options and does not expand the remote launch payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Payload preparation and remote configuration readiness precede the channel create-process call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K explicit commands, P terminal profiles, F workspace folders, and launch environment/configuration size; no new multiplicative factor from the number of tabs or groups.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing awaited launch stages are sequential within each creation. Separate user requests may overlap; this diff adds no batch or collection-wide launch scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the unchanged profile readiness/cached profile state and throttled refresh. Remote shell-environment handling continues through existing authority resolution; the diff introduces neither cache invalidation nor new retry/negative-cache behavior. Xterm constructor promise remains shared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected remote backend createProcess and RemoteTerminalChannelClient payload construction/channel call, in addition to the shared creation path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency and workspace/environment sizes vary; neither request count nor serialization policy changes per equivalent terminal creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new UI entry reuses the established remote operation without increasing effective fan-out or serialized data per terminal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use a contributed default terminal profile or existing terminal-editor commands after optional index forwarding
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contributed creation uses the existing activateByEvent and registered profile-provider callback, then existing focus readiness. Native existing callers still open through TerminalEditorService with undefined index unless they explicitly supply one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate the selected terminal-profile extension and invoke its registered provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected provider invocation per requested contributed terminal, not one per available profile. The unsupported-process fallback loop is not enabled by the new menu, which requires processSupported.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing terminal-editor commands selected and invoked the same provider through createTerminal; the new action adds only another explicit invocation route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Activation and provider completion are awaited for contributed creation. Existing general onTerminal activation remains part of ordinary terminal creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit creation commands and the selected provider's existing implementation; no added per-profile loop or retained history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing provider activation/callback ordering is retained. Optional index forwarding introduces no additional asynchronous operation, cancellation policy, or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Extension activation, profile-provider registration maps, resource-to-editor-input caching, and instance cleanup remain owned by existing services. No cache key includes the new index and no new cache or listener is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged dispatch/ordering and undefined-index behavior, based on the shared service implementation and complete changed hunks; provider-internal cost is not inferred.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension-specific creation cost is outside this diff and was not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing callers retain their placement behavior and contributed profiles retain their existing creation cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all five changed files and every diff page, with targeted caller, menu, cache, lifecycle, local/remote backend, and serialization tracing. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was established. Static read-only review; no profiling or execution.
